feed.title: Cholera Tracker: Global
feed.subtitle: Independent, sourced tracker of cholera worldwide in 2026: WHO case and death counts, countries reporting cases, how this year compares with 2025, WHO's risk level and a dated timeline.

entry.title: ECDC: 291,272 cases worldwide this year
entry.summary: ECDC's monthly overview counts 291,272 cholera cases, including 2,471 deaths, from 1 January to 27 October. In the month since 28 September it recorded 42,136 new cases and 501 new deaths, with Nigeria, DR Congo and South Sudan reporting the most new cases. ECDC says the risk for travellers to affected countries remains low. ECDC's totals are a separate count from the WHO figures above.

Sources: ECDC: cholera worldwide overview (27 Oct)

entry.title: Zambia declares a new cholera outbreak and starts oral vaccination
entry.summary: Zambia's government declared a new cholera outbreak after 304 cases and 11 deaths across seven districts in five provinces, local media reported on 1 October. It is separate from the outbreak the government declared over in July. On 17 October the health ministry's figures, reported by Lusaka Times and Xinhua, were 966 cases and 25 deaths in 12 districts across five provinces, as the country launched an oral cholera vaccination campaign in Lusaka and Chibombo district.
entry.content:

Sources: Diggers, Zambia Monitor, Xinhua, Lusaka Times, Xinhua (July outbreak ended)

entry.title: WHO: DR Congo has 51,412 suspected cholera cases this year
entry.summary: WHO data reported by UN News count 51,412 suspected cases and 1,487 deaths in 21 provinces since the start of 2026. Cases and deaths rose in the week of 21 to 28 September, while DR Congo is also responding to its Ebola outbreak.

entry.title: WHO: suspected cholera cases in Yemen roughly triple in three weeks
entry.summary: WHO says Yemen has recorded 8,034 suspected cholera cases and 27 deaths so far this year, and that weekly cases roughly tripled over three weeks. Five governorates hosting large numbers of displaced people (Abyan, Lahij, Al Dhale'e, Taiz and Aden) account for 92% of reported cases. WHO called for funding and access to safe water, vaccination and health services.

entry.title: WHO: 275,284 cases and 2,601 deaths in 28 countries
entry.summary: WHO's August update, now published in its Weekly Epidemiological Record, covers 1 January to 30 August: 43% fewer cases and 58% fewer deaths than a year earlier. August's 41,915 new cases were 25% fewer than July's. Nigeria (69,263) and DR Congo (44,773) report the most cases in Africa.

entry.title: WHO: 160,799 suspected cases in the African Region, risk high
entry.summary: WHO's regional rapid risk assessment, dated 2 October, counts 160,799 suspected cholera cases and 2,466 deaths in 19 countries of the African Region from 1 January to 20 September, and rates the regional risk high. WHO names Cameroon, Chad, DR Congo, Nigeria and South Sudan as the countries of greatest concern, and says reporting delays affect the most recent weeks.

entry.title: WHO: 2025 had the most cholera deaths since 1999
entry.summary: 47 countries reported 451,499 cases and 7,870 deaths to WHO in 2025. Deaths rose 30% although fewer cases were reported, and seven countries accounted for about 90% of cases and deaths. WHO says the true burden is substantially higher.
entry.content:

Sources: WHO, Down To Earth, The Guardian Nigeria

entry.title: ECDC: 249,136 cases worldwide this year
entry.summary: ECDC's monthly overview counts 249,136 cases, including 1,970 deaths, from 1 January to 28 September, against 436,268 cases and 4,449 deaths at the same point in 2025. In the month to 28 September it recorded 46,153 new cases and 140 deaths; Afghanistan (34,378), DR Congo (8,505) and Yemen (1,885) reported the most cases. ECDC's totals are a separate count from the WHO figures above.

entry.title: UNICEF: cholera is spreading across borders in West and Central Africa
entry.summary: UNICEF says outbreaks are accelerating in six countries: DR Congo, the Republic of the Congo, Nigeria, Chad, Cameroon and the Central African Republic. It reports more than 50,000 cases and 338 deaths in Nigeria this year, and more than 30,400 cases and nearly 700 deaths in DR Congo. The same strain is circulating in Chad, Cameroon and Nigeria around Lake Chad. UNICEF asks for $15 million for the next six months.
